case_title: MOHIT ALIAS SONU AND ANOTHER v. STATE OF U.P. AND ANOTHER
trial_court_outcome: Order rejecting application to summon accused
high_court_outcome: Set aside trial court order and directed to summon accused
neutral_facts: The complainant, Deepak, lodged an FIR naming seven persons as accused regarding an occurrence which took place on 7th February, 2003 at 10.30 p.m. stating that the accused persons named in the FIR armed with lathi, danda and hockey caused injuries to his uncle Kamta Prasad as well as to the complainant. The complainant was medically examined on 8th February, 2003 and a lacerated wound of 4 cm x 0.8 cm scalp deep on left side back of his skull was reported by the doctor. Kamta Prasad succumbed to his injuries alleged to have been caused by the accused. The accused were named in the FIR vide Case Crime No. 44/03 under Sections 147, 323, 504, 506, 304 of the Indian Penal Code. The injured complainant as well as other witnesses were examined by the Investigating Officer, but the Investigating Officer submitted a charge-sheet only against five accused leaving the names of two accused who are the appellants before us. After committal of the case for trial, the trial court examined the complainant as PW-1. In his examination-in-chief, the complainant specifically stated the role of the appellants herein in the occurrence. The complainant then moved an application under Section 319 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for summoning the appellants herein as accused in the case. However, the trial court disposed of the application in view of the fact that cross-examination of PW-1 had not completed and the fact had not been cleared from the witness that there existed probability of the conviction of the appellants herein. A Criminal Miscellaneous Application was filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. before the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad against the above order, and the High Court found no error in the order passed by the trial court as the trial court had not finally decided the question of summoning the appellants and had simply postponed the issue as it thought that the matter should receive its due and proper consideration only after the cross-examination of the witness is over. Subsequently, PW-2 Vivek and PW-3 Deepak Kumar Dubey were also examined apart from the complainant. The second application filed under Section 319, Cr.P.C. was also rejected by the trial court after considering various legal pronouncements, discussing the statements of PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 and finding out that the evidence on record is improper and contradictory. Challenging this order, the complainant again filed a Criminal Miscellaneous Application under Section 482, Cr.P.C. which was allowed by the High Court holding that the lower court committed error in rejecting the application of the complainant for summoning the accused-appellants herein despite the prima facie evidence adduced by the prosecution disclosing their involvement in the alleged occurrence for which the other accused are facing the trial on the same facts of the case.
